info.desc: Amazing Grace is a live album by Aretha Franklin, released on June 1, 1972, by Atlantic Records. It was recorded in January 1972 at the New Temple Missionary Baptist Church in Los Angeles, with Reverend James Cleveland and the Southern California Community Choir accompanying Franklin in performance. Amazing Grace was remastered and re-released in 1999 as a two-compact disc set with many previously unreleased takes. A film documenting the making of the album premiered in 2018. .

podcast.body: This ambitious multimedia project, recorded live over two nights in January 1972 at the New Temple Missionary Baptist Church in Los Angeles, was a critical and commercial triumph. It blended elements of her gospel and pop worlds, featuring rock accompanists like bassist Chuck Rainey and drummer Bernard Purdy, along with the Southern California Community Choir and James Cleveland. Marvin Gaye praised it as "Aritha's singular masterpiece," and it remarkably cracked the top 10 on the Billboard pop album chart, reaching number seven by July of '72. Selling a million copies initially and later certified double platinum by the RIAA, it remains Franklin's top-selling album and the best-selling live gospel LP of all time. "Amazing Grace cracked the top 10 on the Billboard pop album chart, extraordinarily rare for a gospel LP, and reached number seven by July of 72."

podcast.body: This double album became Aretha Franklin's highest-selling LP, representing her boldest display of cultural power and music business clout. Despite generating no top 40 pop hits, it was a full-on gospel album and served as the soundtrack for a film that would not be released until decades after her death. "She released what would become her highest selling LP, a double album that generated no top 40 hits and soundtracked a film that wouldn't see the light of day until decades later."
